title: Scheduled flow suites ran blind: the host's VPN dropped Go TLS handshakes while curl still worked
service: echopoint-investigation routine (prod-org dogfood suites on dev APIs)
summary: The 05:08Z scheduled run of the anchor and echopoint dogfood suites checked **0 of 68 flows**. Both tags exited 3 before launching anything: the CLI could not finish a TLS handshake with `api.echopoint.dev`. The laptop that hosts the suites routes IPv4 through a VPN tunnel, and on that path TLS handshakes from Go, Python and OpenSSL got no answer for an hour or more, even with a 166-byte ClientHello. SecureTransport curl on the same path still worked, so the usual `/health` probe said the network was fine. `run_suites.sh` now probes the control plane with the CLI itself and stops with `NETWORK-DOWN` instead of reporting `pass 0 fail 0`. Product coverage did not change: the CI post-deploy gate had run the anchor suite green on the same commits at 04:21Z.

impact.text: One scheduled suite run produced no result. No customer impact and no product signal lost: dev and prod already served the commits the CI gate had tested. About 60 min of routine time went to diagnosis instead of coverage.

trigger: At 05:08:17Z `run_suites.sh` started both tags; each `flows run --tag` timed out on `POST https://api.echopoint.dev/flows/search` and exited 3.
detection: The routine read `anchor: exit 3 pass 0 fail 0` at 05:09:56Z. The cause took longer: a curl `/health` probe answered 200 in 40 ms, which pointed away from the network until Go, Python and OpenSSL handshakes were tested one by one.
resolution: No mitigation was in the routine's reach: changing the host's VPN is a system setting for a human. The run was closed as blind. `run_suites.sh` gained a CLI-based reachability preflight that waits up to 10 min and then exits 4 with `NETWORK-DOWN`, the default-route interface and the curl result.

events.label: Last suite run green on this host (anchor 28, echopoint 39)
events.detail: Recorded in the routine's run log.

events.label: VPN log starts: tunnel up, NetShield 2, split-tcp on
events.detail: Earliest line of the rotated ProtonVPN log; the connect time itself is not in the log.

events.label: CI gate runs the anchor suite green on 206b6eed
Both tags exit 3: flows/search times out
events.detail: `Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers`; no flow launched.

events.label: Routine reads `exit 3 pass 0 fail 0` and the CLI log
Rerun fails the same way: `TLS handshake timeout`
curl /health 200 in 40 ms; IPv6 path dead; gh fails
events.detail: curl uses SecureTransport and falls back to IPv4. `gh` (Go) also gets `TLS handshake timeout` on api.github.com.

events.label: 10-min recovery poll ends: CLI still down
OpenSSL, Python TLS 1.2/1.3 fail; 1400-byte DF ping passes
events.detail: `openssl s_client` writes a 166-byte ClientHello and reads 0 bytes from 172.64.80.1, so packet size is not the cause.

events.label: 15-min recovery poll ends: CLI still down
Run closed as blind; next run re-probes at 11:08Z
events.detail: The CLI still timed out at 06:07Z. The next scheduled run stops with `NETWORK-DOWN` if the path is still broken.

whys.problem: The 05:08Z scheduled suite run checked 0 of 68 flows; the routine had no suite result for that window

because.text: Both tags exited 3 before launching: the CLI's first request to the control plane never completed TLS
because.evidence: `error: search flows by tag: Post "https://api.echopoint.dev/flows/search": net/http: TLS handshake timeout` in `anchor.log` and `echopoint.log` of the run

because.text: On this host, Go, Python and OpenSSL TLS handshakes got 0 bytes back from every tested HTTPS host; SecureTransport curl did not
because.evidence: `openssl s_client -tls1_2` to 172.64.80.1: `read 0 bytes and written 166 bytes`; `curl -4` same IP: 200, TLS done in 36 ms; Python `ssl` TimeoutError for TLS 1.2 and 1.3

because.text: Packet size is not the cause: 1400-byte DF pings pass and a 166-byte ClientHello also gets no answer
because.evidence: `ping -D -s 1372 172.64.80.1`: 0% loss; `GODEBUG=tlsmlkem=0` (smaller Go hello) still times out

because.text: The IPv4 default route is a VPN tunnel with NetShield and split-tcp on; which part drops non-Apple handshakes is unconfirmed
because.evidence: `netstat -rn`: default via utun7 (10.2.0.2, MTU 1420); ProtonVPN log: `netshield-level: 2`, `split-tcp: true`

because.text: The suite's network path is whatever the laptop's owner configured for personal use that day
because.evidence: The suites run on the CLI's embedded runner on the developer laptop (Run notes; 2026-10-17 host-sleep postmortem A3 still open)

because.text: Scheduled suites run on a personal laptop, so its VPN, Wi-Fi and sleep settings decide if a run can happen
The run reported `exit 3 pass 0 fail 0` twice and took about an hour to name as a host network fault
`run_suites.sh` checked auth expiry and kept the host awake, but never proved the CLI could reach the API
because.evidence: `run_suites.sh` before this change: preflight checks `expires_at` only; its transport rerun handles failed flows, not a launch that selected none

because.text: The suite script assumed the control plane was reachable and had no distinct outcome for a launch-time network failure
The first network check, curl `/health`, passed and pointed the diagnosis away from the network
because.evidence: curl 8.7.1 (SecureTransport) to `api.echopoint.dev/health`: 200 in 40 ms while the CLI timed out

because.text: Reachability was probed with a different TLS stack than the client under test, and nothing said that probe can mislead

contributing: IPv6 was also black-holed on the host, and GitHub DNS failed for about 20 minutes, which hid the TLS pattern behind more general noise.
The VPN log rotates and starts at 04:09Z, so when the tunnel or its features changed after the last green run (23:08Z) is not on record.

well: The run did not report a red suite or file product bugs: `exit 3` with zero flows was read as a launch failure, not as test results.
Testing the handshake with four TLS clients and two packet sizes separated a host-path fault from an MTU or server fault in minutes.
wrong: A curl health check stood in for the CLI's reachability; it passed while the CLI could not connect at all.
Two fixed-length recovery polls (10 and 15 min) spent the run's time without new information.
lucky: The CI post-deploy gate had run the anchor suite green on the same commits 47 min earlier, so no merged change went untested.
anchor#284 and #287 had already been covered by another session; a merge that needed new flows would have gone uncovered this run.
git (SecureTransport) and the REST API through curl still reached GitHub, so the fix and this report could still ship while `gh` could not.

actions.what: Decide the suite host: an always-on machine on a plain network, or Cloud launches for the scheduled runs (same decision as the 2026-10-17 A3)
Until A1: exclude `*.echopoint.dev` and `*.tryanchor.dev` from the VPN tunnel on the suite host, or confirm which VPN feature drops the handshakes
`run_suites.sh` probes the control plane with the CLI itself, waits up to 10 min, then exits 4 with `NETWORK-DOWN`, the route interface and the curl result
flow-suite-testing: probe reachability with the client that runs the suite, since another TLS stack can pass where it fails

messaging.internal: Scheduled flow suites (05:08Z) checked 0 flows: on the suite laptop the VPN path drops Go/OpenSSL TLS handshakes; curl still works. No product signal lost (CI gate green at 04:21Z). run_suites.sh now stops with NETWORK-DOWN. Needed: decide the suite host, or exclude the API hosts from the VPN.
messaging.external: None: dev and CI tooling only.
